headline: Bank of Canada Holds at 2.25% as May Unemployment Sits at 6.6% and Housing Starts Reach 279,317 SAAR
executive_summary:
The Bank of Canada held the overnight rate at 2.25% on June 10, the second consecutive hold, paired with the June Monetary Policy Report — the 5Y Government of Canada benchmark sits at 3.04%, the residential mortgage-renewal anchor, while the 2s10s spread sits +64 basis points and has bull-flattened over both the one-month and one-year windows.1 All 6,426 active Canadian projects ($1,536.5B aggregate) finance against the GoC yield curve anchored by the policy rate, and 257 residential projects ($36.2B) price renewals against the 5Y tenor.2

Statistics Canada reported real GDP at basic prices contracted 0.1% m/m in March 2026, released May 15, with an April flash estimate of +0.4% — manufacturing (NAICS 31-33) advanced 0.4% m/m but remained -2.5% y/y, while construction (NAICS 23) fell 0.6% m/m and -1.5% y/y.3 The manufacturing reading links to 346 active manufacturing projects ($70.0B); the construction reading links to 1,497 active infrastructure projects ($214.0B).3 Mining and oil and gas (NAICS 21) fell 2.1% m/m and -1.5% y/y, mapping to 532 mining and 89 oil and gas projects totalling $246.6B.3

The May Labour Force Survey, released June 6, recorded the unemployment rate at 6.6%, the participation rate at 65.0%, and the employment rate at 60.7% — average hourly wages fell 1.4% m/m to $37.24, reflecting a composition shift in which accommodation and food employment rose 4.3% m/m to 1,204,200 positions and retail employment fell 1.8% m/m to 2,237,500 positions.4 CMHC reported May housing starts at 279,317 SAAR, up 6.9% m/m, with the April unadjusted total at 21,805 units (+33.0% m/m); the new housing price index fell 0.4% m/m in April, the first negative print after consecutive flat-to-rising months.17

The week ahead carries a dense calendar of releases that will reset the inflation and rate picture — Statistics Canada publishes formal May CPI on June 17, the FOMC announces its rate decision and Summary of Economic Projections the same day under new Chair Kevin Warsh, and the Bank of England Monetary Policy Committee meets June 18 with Bank Rate at 3.75%.52128 The European Central Bank raised its deposit facility +25 basis points to 2.25% effective June 17, narrowing the ECB-BoC deposit differential to zero.26

national.analysis:
Statistics Canada's March 2026 monthly GDP print, released May 15, recorded a 0.1% m/m contraction at basic prices, with an April advance flash estimate of +0.4% — twenty NAICS industry readings show goods-producing sector weakness concentrated in mining and oil and gas (NAICS 21) at -2.1% m/m and -1.5% y/y, and in construction (NAICS 23) at -0.6% m/m and -1.5% y/y, against services-producing strength in wholesale trade (+1.8% m/m), arts, entertainment and recreation (+2.0% m/m), and public administration (+0.4% m/m).3 Manufacturing (NAICS 31-33) advanced 0.4% m/m but remained -2.5% y/y, linking to 346 active manufacturing projects ($70.0B) in the project database.3

The May Labour Force Survey, released June 6, recorded unemployment at 6.6%, unchanged m/m, with the participation rate at 65.0% and the employment rate at 60.7% — sector employment shifted toward lower-wage industries, with accommodation and food rising 4.3% m/m to 1,204,200, agriculture rising 8.6% m/m to 240,100, and construction rising 0.5% m/m, while retail trade fell 1.8% m/m to 2,237,500, manufacturing fell 0.5% m/m to 243,200, and mining and oil and gas fell 0.5% m/m to 343,000.4 Average hourly wages fell 1.4% m/m to $37.24, a reading consistent with the composition shift.9

Manufacturing sales reached $77,052.9 million in April, up 4.2% m/m, and wholesale trade reached $138,830.0 million, up 2.8% m/m — both readings sit above their three-month moving averages and link respectively to 346 manufacturing and to broader transport and warehousing project flows tracked across 628 active projects ($54.0B).67 April merchandise exports stood at $66.3 billion per the StatCan section, with energy exports up 9.7% m/m to $19.88 billion and agri-food exports up 8.9% m/m, while mineral exports fell 7.9% m/m.14 The energy export strength sits against a WTI tape down 11.7% w/w to $80.58/bbl, which the cross-reference engine links to 89 active oil and gas projects ($63.2B).37

CMHC reported May housing starts at 279,317 SAAR, up 6.9% m/m from 261,377 SAAR in April, with the April unadjusted total at 21,805 units (singles 3,063, multi 18,742) — multi-unit starts rose 34.3% m/m and single starts rose 25.4% m/m relative to March.17 Residential permits fell 5.5% m/m to $7,482.9 million and non-residential permits fell 10.5% m/m to $5,008.2 million in April per Statistics Canada 34-10-0292, while the new housing price index fell 0.4% m/m to 121.1 in April, the first negative print after flat-to-rising months.810 The headline housing starts reading links to 257 residential projects ($36.2B) in the project database.17

Statistics Canada's quarterly household income, consumption and saving release for Q1 2026 recorded the household savings rate at 3.5%, down 0.2 percentage points q/q from 3.7% in Q4 2025, with household disposable income at $1,811,968 million (+0.6% q/q) — non-residential capital expenditure intentions for 2026 stand at $401,203 million, up 3.7% y/y per Statistics Canada 34-10-0035.1112 The Department of Finance Spring Economic Update 2026 set out $51 billion in infrastructure commitments alongside a new sovereign fund and an expansion of the Investment Tax Credit to cover CCUS-EOR, which the cross-reference engine maps against 1,497 active infrastructure projects ($214.0B) and the broader power and energy sector that tracks 936 active projects ($614.3B).1819

consumer_pulse:
Headline CPI sits at +2.8% y/y on the May reference snapshot while average hourly wages fell 1.4% m/m to $37.24 in the May Labour Force Survey — the gap between price and wage readings continues to surface in cost-of-living trackers, with cost of living, housing affordability, and inflation among the highest-frequency topics this week.45 The household savings rate fell to 3.5% in Q1 2026 from 3.7% in Q4 2025 per Statistics Canada 36-10-0112, the lowest reading in two quarters.12

Mortgage and housing-cost signals dominate the consumer picture — the 5Y Government of Canada yield at 3.04% is the residential mortgage-renewal anchor, down 15 basis points y/y, while the new housing price index fell 0.4% m/m in April, the first negative print after flat-to-rising months.110 CMHC reported May housing starts at 279,317 SAAR, up 6.9% m/m, with multi-unit starts up 34.3% m/m relative to March.17

Energy and food prices shape the goods basket — WTI crude fell 11.7% w/w to $80.58/bbl from $105.42 a month ago, a partial reversal of the recent supply-shock premium, with pass-through to retail gasoline pending.37 Sector employment shifted toward lower-wage industries, with accommodation and food up 4.3% m/m and retail down 1.8% m/m in May, a composition that helps explain the m/m drop in average hourly wages.4 The Department of Finance Spring Economic Update 2026 committed $51 billion in infrastructure spending, established a new sovereign fund, and expanded the Investment Tax Credit to CCUS-EOR, signals that show up in the federal budget and infrastructure topics tracked across the week.18

global.analysis:
The Federal Open Market Committee meets June 16-17 with a Summary of Economic Projections, the first decision under new Chair Kevin Warsh after Jerome Powell exited May 15 — the federal funds target range stands at 3.50-3.75% and a hold is widely priced into futures, sustaining a Fed-BoC differential of approximately +125 basis points (US ceiling 3.75% versus BoC 2.25%) and a CAD/USD reading of 0.7148.21 Core CPI at +2.6% y/y on the March reference (BLS April 15 release) compares to +2.8% a year prior, and the May unemployment rate at 4.4% sits 0.1 percentage points above the April reading.2324

The Philadelphia Fed Survey of Professional Forecasters recorded Q1 2026 GDP at +2.6% with a full-year 2026 forecast of +2.5%, and Q1 private payroll growth ran more than 2.5x the 2025 monthly average — the CUSMA review remains open and a Trump administration 100% tariff threat over Canada-China dealings overhangs 346 active Canadian manufacturing projects ($70.0B) tracked in the project database.22 The next US labour reading, the June Employment Situation, publishes July 2, one week before the Bank of Canada July 9 rate decision.24

global.analysis:
The China National Bureau of Statistics May Manufacturing PMI stood at 50.0, down 0.3 points m/m, with the production sub-index at 51.2 and the new orders sub-index at 49.9, the latter in contraction — the Composite PMI rose 0.4 points to 50.5, with high-technology manufacturing at 52.9 and equipment manufacturing at 52.1.25 Large enterprises printed 51.1 while small and medium enterprises printed 48.5-48.6, an SME-skew divergence echoed in the Caixin private survey beat of consensus.25 The People's Bank of China held the 1-year Loan Prime Rate at 3.10% at the May 20 fixing.25

USD/CNY stood at 6.76, down 1.8% y/y on a yuan-stronger basis — copper at $6.51/lb, up 15.7% y/y per timeseries.json, and the iron ore proxy reflect sustained China industrial demand framing. The project database tracks 532 active Canadian mining projects ($183.4B) and 935 active power and energy projects ($614.3B) downstream of Asian metals demand.37

global.analysis:
The European Central Bank raised the deposit facility rate +25 basis points to 2.25% effective June 17, the first hike in three years, on the June 11 decision — the main refinancing rate sits at 2.40% and the marginal lending rate at 2.65%. President Christine Lagarde cited the Iran-war oil-price spike to four-year highs as the operative motivation for the move.26 The hike narrows the ECB-BoC deposit differential to zero, with both anchored at 2.25%.126

Eurostat reported HICP at +3.2% y/y in April, the highest reading since 2023, with core HICP at +2.5% — Q1 2026 GDP printed -0.2% q/q and the Survey of Professional Forecasters full-year 2026 forecast stands at +0.9%.27 EUR/USD trades at 1.1600, up 0.1% y/y, and the DAX closed at 24,635.30 on June 12, up 10.5% y/y per timeseries.json.37

global.analysis:
The Bank of England Monetary Policy Committee set Bank Rate at 3.75% on April 30 by an 8-1 vote, with the single dissenter voting to hike — the June 18 MPC meeting is expected to hold per market pricing, with the Bank of England central projection placing CPI at 3.1% in Q2 2026, rising to 3.3% in Q3, before easing toward the 2% target over the projection horizon.28 GBP/USD closed at 1.3408 the week ending June 14, down 1.6% y/y per timeseries.json.37

The UK-Canada policy-rate differential sits at +150 basis points (UK Bank Rate 3.75% versus BoC overnight 2.25%) — the United Kingdom is a destination market for Canadian gold (up 26.9% y/y per timeseries.json), uranium, and select agricultural exports, channels tracked through the Canadian mining (532 active projects, $183.4B) and agriculture (463 active projects, $0.3B) sector counts.12837
